sources.title: Adoption of roads by highway authorities
sources.verified_claim: DfT guidance explains how roads may become highways maintainable at public expense under the Highways Act 1980; an adoption mechanism is not evidence that a candidate frontage is already adopted.

sources.title: Road adoption
sources.verified_claim: Enfield publishes its maintained-road register and offers formal written confirmation/plan searches; Section 38 and Section 278 agreements describe adoption and alteration processes, not completed status by themselves.

sources.title: Highways Register (list of Council maintained roads)
sources.verified_claim: Havering states its highways register is live and advises formal extent searches to confirm exact adopted-highway extents; downloaded copies may become stale.

sources.title: Road construction (Sections 38 and 278)
sources.verified_claim: Havering describes Section 38 as the route for offering new roads for adoption and Section 278 for works to existing public highway; agreement process is distinct from final adoption status.

sources.title: List of streets
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth publishes names, locations and an indication of maintenance responsibility for streets in the National Street Gazetteer; list status alone does not prove exact highway boundary at a parcel.

sources.title: Street works register
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth maintains a register of planned street works with dates, locations and responsible organisations; temporary works do not establish permanent access rights or adoption.

sources.title: Stopping up orders
sources.verified_claim: A made stopping-up order can remove public-highway status from carriageway or footway for redevelopment; candidate impact requires exact location and order matching.

sources.title: Road works
sources.verified_claim: Enfield coordinates, permits and inspects current street and road works and points users to live roadworks mapping; temporary works information is operational context, not legal highway extent.
